claims.text: Conventional W–Cu composites have a relatively random dispersion of copper in a tungsten matrix.
Controlled thermomechanical processing, directional solidification, or tailored heat treatment can promote a co-continuous, percolated copper network in a tungsten matrix.
Continuous copper pathways minimize interfacial thermal resistance.
The tungsten matrix continues to provide mechanical strength after formation of a continuous copper network.
The tungsten matrix continues to provide irradiation resilience after formation of a continuous copper network.
Uninterrupted copper channels enhance effective thermal transport.
The thermal-transport enhancement arises from reduced phonon scattering at phase boundaries.
The thermal-transport enhancement arises from reduced electron scattering at phase boundaries.
Tungsten has inherent hardness.
Tungsten has inherent irradiation resistance.
Retention of the tungsten phase prevents the processing intervention from compromising durability and structural integrity.
The processed composite will have higher thermal conductivity than an otherwise comparable conventional W–Cu composite.
The thermal-conductivity increase is likely to be on the order of tens of percent.
The processed composite will retain mechanical durability relative to the conventional composite.
The processed composite will retain irradiation resistance relative to the conventional composite.
Randomly distributed copper phases in conventional W–Cu composites produce higher interfacial thermal resistance than a percolated copper network.
Randomly distributed copper phases provide less continuous heat-conduction pathways than a percolated copper network.
The predicted benefit should hold under the high-temperature and high-flux irradiation conditions typical of fusion-reactor joint applications.
The predicted benefit depends on forming an interconnected copper network and remaining within typical thermal and irradiation-flux ranges for fusion-reactor joints.
Processing-induced defects could adversely affect mechanical or irradiation performance.
